Complete the arguments in the reasoning below to find the Laplace transform of f(t)=e−t.First, we apply the definition of the Laplace transform:

∫0∞e(−1−s)tdt
∫−∞∞e(−1+s)tdt
∫0∞e(−1+s)tdt
∫−∞∞e(−1−s)tdt
∫0∞e(−1−s)tdt
L{f(t)}=F(s)={(∫−∞∞e(−1+s)tdt)(S0)}

We now examine the convergence of F(s) for different values of s:

For
 
s>−1
s≤−1
the integral is divergent.

For
 
s≤−1
s≥−1
s>−1
the integral is convergent.
